exposure: Occurrence of obstetrical anal sphincter injury (OASI)
Trial of labor after cesarean (TOLAC) in women with no prior vaginal delivery
outcome: Maternal and intrapartum characteristics associated with OASI
cohort: 2061 women undergoing TOLAC with no prior vaginal delivery between March 2011 and June 2020
finding: Gestational age at delivery was the only predictor of OASI among women with no prior vaginal deliveries undergoing TOLAC, with a 1.1% incidence rate comparable to primiparous women.
mod_finding: The incidence of obstetrical anal sphincter injury (OASI) in women without prior vaginal deliveries undergoing a trial of labor after cesarean (TOLAC) is 1.1% and does not differ from that of primiparous women.
gest_age: Mean gestational age at TOLAC was lower in the OASI group (39(0/7) ± 1(2/7) vs. 39(5/7) ± 1(2/7), p = 0.012).
